MT 1:1 runs 16 tokens and MT 2:1 runs 9: the seven-token regnal window בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.1, byte tier) has no counterpart in 2:1, so the header-noun class is not the sole discriminator - the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative says as much ('names a distinct royal-regnal frame absent from verse 2'), and the word order differs too (1:1 חֲזוֹן֙ + name + patronym + אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה; 2:1 הַדָּבָר֙ + אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה + name). The same paragraph's untiered two-site framing of the relative clause also understates it: אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה is byte-identical at THREE verses - oshb:Isa.1.1, oshb:Isa.2.1 and oshb:Isa.13.1 (sweep: 3 verses, byte) - the third being the massa hinge.

findings.proposed_cure: Strike 'only ... the sole discriminator' and restate the contrast as the regnal-window presence/absence plus the header-noun class, citing the relative clause at its true three-verse byte census.
